props.topic: AI1 CLI · CUT TO THE BLUEPRINT
props.command: Explain how to cut a signed book plan's scope down honestly: the evidence a cut needs, the log every exclusion requires, and how to handle a disagreement without letting it drift silently.
output: what you cut is usually fine — that's exactly why it's hard
a cut with no log entry is a disappearance, not a decision
silent drift is the one forbidden move

beats.act: Act I — The Power of No, Made Accountable
beats.narration_text: Cutting is harder than writing, because what you cut is usually fine. It's competent, finished, someone's real work — it just doesn't serve the reader your Blueprint actually named.

beats.act: Act I — The Power of No, Made Accountable
beats.narration_text: Cut because you're bored of a chapter, and the decision dies with your mood. Cut because the Editorial Review and the signed plan agree it doesn't serve the reader, and the decision survives being questioned later.

beats.act: Act II — Cut Per the Plan
beats.narration_text: A real blueprint, drafted in 1913, names every room before a single wall goes up. This book's own Blueprint works exactly that way — it named a disposition for every one of twenty-four inherited chapters before any cut was actually made.

beats.narration_text: Individual chapters, judged one at a time, landed at zero wholly cut — every one of them converts, merges, demotes, or splits. The one true deletion ran a different way: the school apparatus itself, gone globally, in a single logged move.

beats.act: Act III — Log Every Exclusion, Disagree Once on Purpose
beats.narration_text: Open the drawer, and every record is exactly where it should be — findable, labeled, accounted for. That's the whole purpose of an exclusion log: the difference between a decision and a disappearance.

shot.prompt: real photo of an open wooden file-cabinet drawer with labeled hanging folders -- illustrative of a logged, filed record, not a literal depiction of this book's exclusion log. Already sourced, see media/A3-1.source.txt

beats.act: Act III — Log Every Exclusion, Disagree Once on Purpose
beats.narration_text: Disagree with the plan, and cut it anyway, or silently keep it, and the disagreement just evaporates, unaccountable either way. Resolve it explicitly instead — amend the plan, logged, or make the cut, logged — and the disagreement itself becomes part of the record.

resolver.label: Silent drift is the one forbidden move

beats.act: Act IV — What Can Go Wrong
beats.narration_text: Cut something because the evidence is merely thin, and you've punished uncertainty as if it were a verdict. Name the real reason instead — 'doesn't serve this reader' — and the cut is finally something you can actually defend.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Cutting is harder than writing because what you cut is usually fine — the discipline is deleting on evidence, against a signed plan, with a logged reason, never on a mood. This book's real cut column: twenty-one chapters convert or merge, two demote to a module, one splits, zero wholly cut — the one global cut was the school apparatus itself, removed everywhere at once. Every exclusion gets a four-field record — what, why, who, and the reopen condition — which is the difference between a decision and a disappearance. And disagreement gets resolved explicitly, never silently: amend the plan, logged, or make the cut, logged — and 'thin evidence' is never a reason by itself. Only 'doesn't serve this reader' is.
